anatomy.intro: Slender ribbed stems branch and lengthen into a scrambling plant.

parts.function: The green cylindrical stem carries a series of low ribs.
parts.label: Slender stem

parts.function: Small felted growing cushions sit closely together along the ribs.
parts.label: Areole

parts.function: Fine pale-to-brown spines radiate from the areoles.
parts.label: Radial spines

parts.function: A new branch adds another extending stem to the scrambling plant.
parts.label: Side branch

flowers.text: White flowers roughly 15–19 cm long emerge near the upper areoles and are followed by red fruits. The fruit’s spines are deciduous: they fall away as the fruit develops.

growth.note: The long, narrow stems eventually lean and scramble, giving an established plant its serpentine outline.

stages.text: Young stems can stand upright in a compact group.
stages.title: Upright start

stages.text: Longer stems branch and begin to lean or arch.
stages.title: Extending branches

stages.text: With age, stems can clamber through supports or trail when unsupported.
stages.title: Scrambling adult

habitat.text: Serpent cactus is native to Mexico, where Kew describes it as a scrambling succulent shrub of seasonally dry tropical habitats. Its slender stems are built for a different life from a compact barrel cactus: the classic botanical description records stems climbing through bushes, trailing over walls or hanging when support is absent.

lookalikes.name: Ming Thing
lookalikes.text: Ming Thing grows in thick irregular clubs. Serpent cactus develops long, narrow ribbed stems that lean and scramble.

mature.text: Developed stems can reach around 3 m long while remaining only about 2–5 cm thick, producing a slender, sprawling plant.

milestones.text: Joined the collection from Costa Farms.
milestones.title: Acquired

nameStory.text: Kew accepts Nyctocereus serpentinus and lists Peniocereus serpentinus as a synonym. Both names are common in cactus references.

sources.title: Britton and Rose — The Cactaceae, volume 2
